requirements: R1: convert a lowercase snake_case status into title-cased words
risks: display_status function: low — pure function, no external callers, no state, no boundaries
invariants: I1: One-word values must still be title-cased (e.g., 'pending' -> 'Pending')
preserved_behaviors: P1: One-word values are title-cased as before

checks_executed.result: No external callers found; only test_status.py references display_status

findings.claim: The test suite does not exercise snake_case inputs with more than one underscore, so a partial snake-case handling bug can pass all tests while violating R1.
evidence: test_status.py:7-8: only snake_case test is display_status('in_progress') == 'In Progress'
test_status.py:10-11: only single-word test is display_status('pending') == 'Pending'
Direct sabotage: return value.replace('_', ' ', 1).title() passes both existing tests but returns 'In Progress_review' for display_status('in_progress_review') instead of 'In Progress Review'.
findings.failure_mechanism: Developer replaces only the first underscore (or otherwise partially splits snake_case) -> multi-word statuses are not fully title-cased -> R1 silently fails for valid inputs allowed by the lowercase-letters-and-underscores constraint.
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code — the actual implementation value.replace('_', ' ').title() at status.py:2 replaces all underscores and correctly handles multi-underscore inputs; verified by reading the source
